title: Tales of the Tendo Family
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In Meiji-era Japan (MangaUpdates), Masato of the powerful Tendo family is to marry a baron's daughter, Hojo Ran, but the bride who arrives is an impostor who took the real Ran's place because no bride is said to leave the Tendo family alive (One Peace Books blurb; SLJ). The stand-in, lonely since the death of the adoptive grandfather who loved her, intends to die with honor, and Masato keeps her at his side amid family feuds and succession intrigue (SLJ; MangaUpdates).
life_message: It suggests that a life given away for others can be met, and changed, by someone who decides that life is worth keeping.

content.note: Murders, attempted murder, assassins and an amputee (MangaUpdates); SLJ mentions Masato's 'sadism'. Detail to verify.
Dark, dangerous household where brides do not survive (blurb); family feud and intrigue.
SLJ notes brief non-graphic nudity. MangaUpdates also tags rape, attempted rape, sexual assault and an incest subplot (single source; capped, to verify).
The heroine's wish to die is central; SLJ advises a trigger warning for suicidal thoughts; MangaUpdates tags attempted suicide.
Self-sacrifice framed as honor; manipulative, possessive male lead (MangaUpdates).

dominant: Self-sacrifice and the worth of a life; oppressive great-family traditions; dark romance

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Family honor, feuds and revenge drive the Tendo house (MangaUpdates).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Rigid household rules and arranged marriage in a Meiji great family.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Clan succession and family feud are the core conflict.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: A distinguished family with servants and heirs; rank governs life.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Tradition and lineage frame every choice.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival in a dangerous household precedes self-expression.

folkways.japan: The Meiji-era great house, arranged marriage, succession and the ideal of dying with honor reflect historical Japanese family (ie) structures and honor culture, depicted rather than endorsed.

delivery.evidence: SLJ interview: readers are left to weigh Ran's motives; characters are morally grey.
delivery.note: The series presents its themes through morally grey characters and leaves judgment of the heroine's motives to readers.

winners_losers: Ran, who expected to die, gains reasons to live beside Masato; the cruelty of the great family is shown as destructive. Ongoing series; outcome not known.
